overall_notes: Pair 4 clears the strict bar with all six categories at Level 4. ALIGNMENT: E1.4 is the only primary expectation and every success criterion (move, turn, give, follow) is named in lesson activities; expanded_walkthrough.rationale explicitly cross-references Lesson 3 (congruence) and Lesson 5 (capstone). PEDAGOGICAL_DEPTH: rotation-amount confusion (quarter vs half) is the named trap, cited to Battista (2007) on spatial reasoning AND Clements & Battista on rotation understanding; recovery_moves provides three diagnostic-branched paths (A: half-when-quarter, B: correct amount/wrong direction, C: rotates correctly but cannot articulate) that a substitute could follow. INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE: puppets are explicitly OPTIONAL with three teacher substitutions named; all other materials are everyday (anchor chart, paper map grids, paper cards, tracker); 12/25/13 = 50 min is realistic for G3; movement-learner differentiation 'Walk a tape grid on floor' plus the body-turn echo at seats provides a no-paper, body-based alternative path. CLARITY_VOICE: Tig and Coco anchor minds_on and consolidation, vocabulary has child-friendly definitions, every success criterion begins with 'I can', and the rotation refrain 'Quarter is 90, half is 180 — that's ROTATION!' is quoted in the hook and chanted 3x in the exit_routine — a memorable, distinctive quotable. MATHEMATICAL_AUTHENTICITY: conceptual progression is explicit (90° = corner of a square; 180° = opposite; 4 quarters = full circle; quarter is half of half); the STRATEGY COMPARE step in action.steps[5] has Pair A 'rotate first, walk second' vs Pair B 'walk first, rotate second' debated by the class with the teacher citing Battista (2007), letting children compare invented strategies. LESSON_WORKSHEET_CONSISTENCY: each worksheet part maps to a named success criterion (Part 1 = FOLLOW, Part 2 = TURN identification, Part 3 = GIVE), image_assets list the same map grid and turn icons used in the lesson, and Part 2's static-icon identification deliberately varies the practice format from the lesson's body-turn demos as a transfer task.
